subject: biology
title: ADH and the control of water content
key_idea: (Separate science) ADH is released by the pituitary gland when the blood is too concentrated. It makes the collecting duct more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed and the urine is smaller in volume and more concentrated. This is negative feedback.

sections.heading: Detecting the water content of the blood

blocks.text: (Separate science) The water content of the blood changes with drinking, sweating and eating. The brain monitors it and sends a hormone message.

items.meaning: A hormone from the pituitary gland that controls how much water the kidney reabsorbs.
The last part of the kidney tubule, where the final amount of water is reabsorbed.

items.text: Receptors in the hypothalamus detect that the blood is too concentrated, because it has too little water.
The hypothalamus sends a message to the pituitary gland.
The pituitary gland releases **ADH** into the blood.
The blood carries ADH to the kidneys, its target organs.

items: The hypothalamus detects the water content of the blood.
The pituitary gland releases ADH into the blood.

blocks.text: ADH acts on the collecting duct. It changes how much water is reabsorbed, so it changes the urine.
Too little water in the blood

items: The collecting duct becomes more permeable to water.
More water is reabsorbed into the blood by osmosis.
The urine is more concentrated and smaller in volume.

blocks.text: Too much water in the blood

items: Less ADH is released, or none.
The collecting duct is less permeable to water.
Less water is reabsorbed, so more stays in the urine.
The urine is more dilute and larger in volume.
More ADH means a more permeable collecting duct, more water reabsorbed and less, concentrated urine.
Less ADH means the reverse: more, dilute urine.

blocks.text: When the blood water content returns to normal, ADH release falls. The change is reversed, so this is negative feedback. Pick a situation to see the response.

diagram.alt: Choose a situation to see how ADH, the collecting duct and the urine respond.

options.label: Hot day, not enough to drink
results: Falls, so the blood is more concentrated
More permeable, so more water is reabsorbed

options.label: Drinking a large volume of water
results: Rises, so the blood is more dilute
Less permeable, so less water is reabsorbed

options.label: A disease that reduces the amount of ADH made
results: Tends to fall, because extra water is lost in the urine
Less water is reabsorbed from the kidney tubule

items: Negative feedback keeps the water content of the blood close to normal.
Too concentrated: more ADH. Too dilute: less ADH.

checks.q: Which gland releases ADH into the blood?
A man has not had a drink all day. Explain how ADH changes his urine.
checks.a: More ADH makes the collecting duct more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed into the blood. The urine is more concentrated and smaller in volume.

checks.q: Explain why less ADH is released after a person drinks a lot of water.
checks.a: The blood water content rises, which is detected by the hypothalamus. This is negative feedback, so the pituitary gland releases less ADH.

worked_example.question:
ADH is a hormone that affects the production and concentration of urine by the kidneys.

Explain how ADH affects the production and concentration of urine by the kidneys.
answer_points: (Increased / high) ADH increases water reabsorption, or increases permeability to water (allow the converse for low or no ADH).
Water is reabsorbed from the kidney tubules.
So ADH increases the concentration of the urine.
So ADH decreases the volume of the urine.
worked_example.tip: Four marks: reabsorption, from the tubules, then concentration up and volume down.

worked_example.question: Describe how the water content of the blood is controlled in the nephron.
answer_points: Water content too low: the hypothalamus detects too little water in the blood.
ADH is released from the pituitary gland into the blood.
The collecting duct becomes more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed into the blood by osmosis.
More concentrated urine and a smaller volume of urine are produced.
Water content too high: the hypothalamus detects too much water, and ADH is lowered or not released.
The collecting duct is less permeable, less water is reabsorbed, and more dilute, larger-volume urine is produced.
worked_example.tip: Marked in levels. Describe both a low and a high water content, and link ADH from the pituitary gland to the collecting duct.

worked_example.question:
ADH is a protein hormone made up of amino acids.

Alcohol inhibits ADH production.

After the alcohol has been removed from a person’s body, control mechanisms will correct the excess loss of water caused by the alcohol.

Describe these control mechanisms.
answer_points: (Low) water potential or decreased water levels are detected by the hypothalamus (ignore: brain).
This causes the release of ADH, or increased ADH levels.
Increased permeability of the collecting duct / kidney tubules, so increased reabsorption of water into the blood, decreased urine production, or more concentrated urine.
worked_example.tip: Two marks from three points. Say hypothalamus, then ADH, then the effect on the kidney tubule.

worked_example.question:
When the body becomes dehydrated, the concentration of urine increases.

Explain the changes that occur in the body that lead to the production of concentrated urine.
answer_points: The hypothalamus detects that the blood is too concentrated (it has a low water content).
ADH makes the collecting duct more permeable.
More water is reabsorbed into the blood.
worked_example.tip: Follow the chain in order: detect, release ADH, collecting duct, water reabsorbed.
